seo.metaDescription: Assess external attack surface validation with VajraX. Review AI-powered evidence, authorised evaluation scope and licensing to guide remediation decisions.

sections.title: VajraX
sections.subtitle: AI-powered exposure validation of your external attack surface.

sections.heading: External attack surface *exposure validation*
sections.body: VajraX is for security teams that need to evaluate exposure on the external attack surface. Identifying a possible exposure starts the review; validation examines the evidence needed to understand it and decide the next action.
sections.secondaryHeading: Review evidence, not just a finding count
sections.secondaryBody:
Use a guided evaluation to inspect the product’s validation approach, its limits and the information available to remediation owners. VajraX sits in our [Cyber Security](/services/cyber-security) portfolio alongside specialist security services.

[Request a guided VajraX demo](#get-in-touch) · [Browse products](/products-and-accelerators)

sections.heading: Evaluate the exposure and its evidence
sections.description: VajraX provides AI-powered exposure validation of your external attack surface. Review supported targets, validation methods and evidence outputs during evaluation.

items.title: External attack-surface scope
items.description: Focus the evaluation on the external assets your organisation is authorised to test. Agree targets, exclusions and ownership before any live assessment.

items.title: AI-powered validation
items.description: Review how AI assists the exposure-validation process, including the method, supporting evidence and limitations. Confirm which decisions require human review.

items.title: Finding review
items.description: Inspect a finding with the security and remediation owners. Agree the evidence needed to assess relevance, handle uncertain findings and decide follow-up.

sections.heading: An authorised validation evaluation
sections.description: Illustrative evaluation workflow: agree the scope, review validation evidence and plan follow-up. Live testing requires explicit authorisation from the asset owner.

items.title: Approve the scope
items.description: Start with a guided walkthrough. Before live testing, obtain authorisation and agree asset scope, exclusions and operational constraints.

items.title: Inspect the validation
items.description: Review a finding and its supporting evidence. Establish where AI assists, where human approval is required and how limitations are recorded.

items.title: Agree the follow-up
items.description: Assign remediation ownership and the evidence needed for closure. Confirm whether and how product-supported revalidation fits the operating process.

sections.heading: Example: reviewing an external exposure
sections.body:
A security owner needs to understand whether a reported external exposure requires remediation. Evaluate VajraX using an authorised sample or guided finding review, then agree the evidence that would support prioritisation and follow-up.

This illustrative pattern is not a client case study or a claim of verified closure.
sections.secondaryBody:
[Regulated Cyber Readiness](/solutions/regulated-cyber-readiness) connects exposure validation, control mapping and remediation evidence. Keep product evidence distinct from compliance decisions; explore [Exposure validation & AppSec](/services/cyber-security/exposure-validation-appsec) for specialist assessment services.

[Request a guided VajraX demo](#get-in-touch). Keep sensitive asset details out of your initial enquiry.

sections.heading: Enterprise fit and licensing
sections.description: Agree the supported estate, operating responsibilities and commercial scope before selecting VajraX.

items.title: Deployment and integrations
items.description: Confirm supported targets, testing modes, integration outputs and deployment or residency requirements. Agree operational safety constraints and the authorised scope before considering a live evaluation.

items.title: Security and responsibility
items.description: Review evidence access, storage, retention and the division of responsibility between your asset owners, the software operator and Linkfields services. Define approvals and escalation before testing.

items.title: Licence and optional services
items.description: Available by licence, subscription or SaaS, with or without Linkfields services. Confirm onboarding, support and any managed-service scope separately, including responsibilities and commercial terms.

sections.note: Licence and subscription describe buying terms; they do not establish which hosting options are available. Confirm deployment, support and inclusion details for your scope.
